title: Q-CTRL Unifies Boulder Opal and Fire Opal into Autonomous End-to-End Quantum Infrastructure Software - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Q-CTRL fused Boulder Opal (autonomous QPU calibration) and Fire Opal (error-suppressed execution) into one hardware-agnostic stack that brought up a 21-qubit QuantWare Contralto-D in hours with 99.95% 1Q fidelity and 13x coherence gains; it runs live on Elevate Quantum's Q-PAC, with cloud access via Quantum Rings in December 2026.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL merged its Boulder Opal hardware characterization/calibration platform with its Fire Opal error-suppressed execution software into a single end-to-end quantum infrastructure workflow, announced November 16, 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Q-CTRL is moving from point tools to a full-stack infrastructure layer, raising its strategic value as a vendor-neutral software control plane.
insights.quote: the integrated software stack automates the full lifecycle from bare quantum processor bring-up to compiled workload execution

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's unified Boulder Opal/Fire Opal stack replaces weeks of manual specialist tuning of quantum processors with automated routines that share real-time hardware state across calibration and compilation layers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Automating QPU bring-up cuts the physics-team labor bottleneck for new hardware vendors and data-center operators.
insights.quote: replacing weeks of manual specialist tuning with automated routines

insights.claim: Linking calibration (Boulder Opal) and execution (Fire Opal) over a shared hardware model lets recalibration parameter updates propagate immediately into circuit compilation, dynamical decoupling, and crosstalk suppression without manual database updates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Tight calibration-to-compiler coupling is a defensible integration moat versus standalone transpilers.

insights.claim: Conventional quantum deployments require dedicated physics teams to characterize qubits, tune gates, maintain drift parameters, and manually sync gate definitions with downstream transpilers when bringing a newly cooled processor online.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals a sizable operational-cost pain point that automation software vendors can monetize.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's unified stack ingests circuits from Qiskit, QASM, and NVIDIA CUDA-Q without requiring user-side language rewrites.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Framework neutrality, including NVIDIA CUDA-Q, positions Q-CTRL to ride hybrid GPU-QPU workflows.
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Unified Boulder Opal & Fire Opal Stack and Hardware Validation (table)

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's stack cross-compiles optimized pulses into the native low-level languages of Quantum Machines and Qblox control electronics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Control-electronics integrations make Q-CTRL a complementary layer for both major independent controller vendors.
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Unified Boulder Opal & Fire Opal Stack and Hardware Validation (table)

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's unified stack supports QPUs from QuantWare, Rigetti, Anyon Computing, Qolab, and Equal1, spanning superconducting transmon and silicon spin architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-modality support (transmon and spin) reduces Q-CTRL's exposure to any single hardware winner; RGTI is among supported platforms.
insights.quote: Covers both superconducting transmon architectures and silicon spin processors.
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Unified Boulder Opal & Fire Opal Stack and Hardware Validation (table)

insights.claim: Boulder Opal autonomously characterized a 21-qubit QuantWare Contralto-D in under 1 hour and calibrated it in under 4 hours, reaching 99.95% median single-qubit and >98% median two-qubit fidelity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hours-not-weeks bring-up is a concrete benchmark for time-to-operational for new QPU installs.
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Unified Boulder Opal & Fire Opal Stack and Hardware Validation (table)

insights.claim: Fire Opal on the QuantWare Contralto-D delivered 13x longer median coherence (1.3 μs to 16.9 μs) and up to 12x higher Bernstein-Vazirani success versus Qiskit L3 optimization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Large software-only gains versus default Qiskit compilation support the thesis that error suppression extracts more value from existing hardware; note benchmarks are vendor-reported.
insights.quote: 13x longer median coherence (1.3 μs to 16.9 μs)
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Unified Boulder Opal & Fire Opal Stack and Hardware Validation (table)

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's unified stack is running live on Elevate Quantum's Q-PAC open-architecture system in Colorado, which pairs QuantWare superconducting hardware with Qblox control electronics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open-architecture regional deployments (modular hardware + third-party control + third-party software) are an emerging go-to-market model to watch.
insights.locator: The unified stack is running live

insights.claim: End-user cloud access to Elevate Quantum's Q-PAC system running Q-CTRL software is scheduled to open in December 2026 through Quantum Rings' Open Quantum platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A near-term catalyst: watch December 2026 launch for usage and uptime evidence of the automated stack.
insights.quote: End-user cloud access to the Q-PAC deployment is scheduled to open in December 2026
insights.locator: The unified stack is running live
